forces.title: European construction output remains subdued
forces.description: Europe's construction output is expected to grow by a marginal 0.5% in 2026, following a decline in 2024. The building sector, encompassing residential and non-residential construction, remains a weak spot due to higher interest rates, increased construction costs, and economic uncertainty. This subdued growth implies a challenging environment for diversified real estate conglomerates pursuing new developments or expansions across their multi-asset portfolios in Europe, limiting opportunities for robust expansion and profitability from new projects.
forces.source_title: Europe's construction sector faces a period of weak growth

forces.title: High financing costs and geopolitical risks cap real estate momentum
forces.description: Higher financing costs, exacerbated by rising interest rates, and increased geopolitical risks stemming from conflicts like the Middle East war, are significantly dampening momentum across Europe's construction and real estate sectors. These factors make new builds less affordable, increase investor caution, and lead to postponement of projects. For diversified real estate conglomerates, this translates into reduced investment appetite, higher capital expenditure, and increased uncertainty for multi-asset development, impacting both project viability and the attractiveness of property acquisitions.
forces.source_title: Europe's construction sector faces a period of weak growth

forces.title: Increasing construction costs erode developer margins
forces.description: Across Belgium, the Netherlands, Ireland, and Norway, rising energy prices, material costs (e.g., concrete, cement, bricks, metals), and labour expenses are pushing up overall construction costs. This makes new-build projects less financially viable as developers struggle to fully pass these increases on to buyers or tenants, particularly when existing properties offer cheaper alternatives. Diversified real estate conglomerates face significant margin pressure and project profitability challenges across their varied development portfolios, compelling them to re-evaluate investment strategies and project feasibility.
forces.source_title: Belgian building permit recovery continues, but challenges lie ahead

forces.title: Infrastructure and regulatory hurdles delay real estate projects
forces.description: New-build projects in the Netherlands face intensifying execution constraints such as grid congestion and nitrogen restrictions, causing delays in delivery. Similarly, Norway experiences low construction activity due to rising costs and regulatory uncertainty. These bottlenecks affect residential, office, and logistics developments. Diversified real estate conglomerates must contend with extended project timelines, increased costs, and reduced efficiency across their multi-asset development pipelines in these markets, necessitating more robust risk management and longer planning horizons for new projects.
forces.source_title: Recovery in Dutch commercial real estate is less robust than it appears

forces.title: Tax changes and rent regulation deter foreign real estate investors
forces.description: Foreign investors have largely exited the Dutch commercial real estate market, particularly the residential segment, due to tax changes (increased transfer tax from 10.4% to 8% for residential, but still high) and new rent regulation. This withdrawal reduces capital flows for residential investment, especially in affordable rental housing, where financial viability is already weak. Diversified real estate conglomerates with significant Dutch residential rental portfolios or development plans face reduced liquidity and investment interest from external partners, complicating financing and market entry/exit strategies.
forces.source_title: Recovery in Dutch commercial real estate is less robust than it appears

forces.title: ESG focus reduces appeal of non-sustainable office properties
forces.description: Institutional investors are increasingly prioritizing societal impact and ESG policies, leading to a decline in interest for outdated office buildings that lack a financially viable sustainability pathway. This trend affects the liquidity and valuation of older assets within diversified real estate portfolios, pushing conglomerates to invest heavily in renovation and sustainability upgrades or face reduced marketability and potential write-downs for non-compliant properties. Maintaining attractive office assets now requires substantial capital expenditure for modern, energy-efficient designs.
forces.source_title: Recovery in Dutch commercial real estate is less robust than it appears

forces.title: E-commerce shift challenges traditional retail real estate
forces.description: The structural shift towards online shopping, potentially accelerated by agentic commerce, continues to impact retail real estate. Investor demand for retail properties in the Netherlands remains concentrated in prime locations with limited vacancy risks, contributing to an overall decline in retail real estate stock. Diversified real estate conglomerates with retail assets face ongoing pressure to adapt their portfolios, focusing on prime, experiential retail or redeveloping underperforming assets to other uses to maintain relevance and profitability in a changing retail landscape.
forces.source_title: Recovery in Dutch commercial real estate is less robust than it appears

forces.title: Geopolitical uncertainty dampens logistics real estate investment
forces.description: Geopolitical tensions are increasing uncertainty around international trade, directly affecting demand for logistics real estate. Investors are becoming more cautious in making acquisitions, and vacancy rates outside traditional hotspots in the Netherlands have risen. Diversified real estate conglomerates with logistics portfolios must prioritize prime locations and properties with sufficient charging infrastructure, as these factors are gaining importance for efficient operations and tenant demand in a challenging market, requiring strategic focus on high-quality assets.
forces.source_title: Recovery in Dutch commercial real estate is less robust than it appears

forces.title: EU infrastructure investment drives specialized construction demand
forces.description: Infrastructure investment, particularly in energy and digital networks, is providing an offset to broader construction sector weakness in the EU. Investments in renewable energy, electricity grid expansion, fibre-optic networks, and 5G deployment are expected to remain strong. For diversified real estate conglomerates, this creates demand for specialized real estate related to these sectors, such as sites for energy infrastructure or telecom towers (classified under specialty RE). This offers an avenue for portfolio diversification and growth in high-demand, infrastructure-linked real estate segments.
forces.source_title: Europe's construction sector faces a period of weak growth

forces.title: Data centre buildout fuels investment and activity
forces.description: Data centre buildout is noted as a significant growth driver in Norway, pulling up investment among service contacts in 2026 and accelerating growth into 2027. Demand for energy supply equipment (cables, transformers) also increases. This robust activity in data centre real estate, driven by AI infrastructure needs and strategic investment, represents a substantial tailwind for diversified real estate conglomerates with holdings or development plans in this high-demand asset class, particularly in regions actively expanding digital infrastructure and computing capacity.
forces.source_title: Regional Network report 3/2026: Minor changes in growth prospects

forces.title: Defence spending creates new demand for logistics real estate
forces.description: Europe's increased defence spending, with NATO members pledging to raise expenditure significantly, is emerging as a credible demand driver for the industrial and logistics property sector. This shift encourages domestic production, expanded stockpiling, and resilient supply chains, potentially adding 8-20% to annual logistics demand. For diversified real estate conglomerates, this provides a new, solid, and long-term demand anchor for their logistics and industrial property holdings, offering opportunities for build-to-suit or long-term lease agreements for specialized, secure facilities and fostering reindustrialization efforts.
forces.source_title: Europe's defence push will boost logistics real estate – but won’t…

forces.title: Retail parks and shopping centres attract strong investor interest in Ireland
forces.description: Investor interest in retail park and shopping centres in Ireland has remained strong, with notable transactions closing across various cities. This is driven by a reinvigoration of in-store retail post-pandemic, leading to international brands opening new stores and occupancy levels returning to over 95%. For diversified real estate conglomerates, this trend signals a positive outlook for the retail component of their portfolios, indicating sustained demand and potential for capital appreciation in well-located and modern retail assets, offsetting some of the broader retail sector headwinds.
forces.source_title: Bank of Ireland Sectors Team — Developments & Insights May 2026

forces.title: AI transforming real estate operations and value chain
forces.description: AI is set to unlock significant value in real estate by transforming processes across the entire property value chain, from discovery and sales to construction scheduling and property management. This goes beyond isolated tools to reimagining business domains, improving efficiency, and enhancing customer experience. Diversified real estate conglomerates adopting AI-enabled workflows and agents can achieve faster operations, personalized guidance, and better insights for pricing and incentives across their multi-asset portfolios, creating a competitive advantage and driving substantial operational and financial gains over the long term.

forces.title: Commercial real estate shifts towards dynamic, short-term optimization
forces.description: The commercial real estate sector is moving away from a purely 'buy-and-hold' model towards one that emphasizes short- and medium-term optimization strategies, akin to commodity trading. Driven by AI/ML making arbitrage detection cheaper and an influx of private equity, this represents a fundamental shift. Diversified real estate conglomerates must adapt by embedding greater optionality, using real-time valuations, and cultivating a culture that embraces calculated risks to capture additional 'dark value' across their varied portfolios, fundamentally changing how real estate assets are managed and traded.
forces.source_title: Taking a Page from Commodity Traders: A New Playbook for Commercial Real Estate Investors

viewpoints.title: Dutch commercial real estate recovery is less robust than it appears
viewpoints.description: Despite a strong Q1 2026 investment volume in Dutch commercial real estate, the underlying recovery is fragile. Rising construction and renovation costs, execution bottlenecks like grid congestion and nitrogen restrictions, and heightened geopolitical uncertainty are weighing on new developments and transaction activity. This subdued momentum cautions diversified real estate conglomerates regarding sustained growth and profitability in their multi-asset portfolios in the Netherlands, particularly concerning new projects and the viability of older assets requiring significant ESG investments.
viewpoints.source_title: Recovery in Dutch commercial real estate is less robust than it appears

viewpoints.title: Commercial real estate investors underutilize short-to-medium term value capture
viewpoints.description: BCG highlights that commercial real estate investors worldwide are missing an estimated $200 billion in annual value by not adopting a more flexible approach to short- and medium-term optimization. The traditional long-term 'buy-and-hold' model, common among diversified real estate conglomerates, leaves significant arbitrage opportunities unexplored. Integrating AI-enabled tools and adapting strategies from commodity traders could unlock substantial returns for multi-asset real estate portfolios by enabling faster reactions to market signals and opportunistic capital deployment.
viewpoints.source_title: Taking a Page from Commodity Traders: A New Playbook for Commercial Real Estate Investors

viewpoints.title: Commercial real estate holds highest potential for short-term value creation
viewpoints.description: A BCG survey of C-suite executives globally identified commercial real estate as having the greatest potential for value creation through short- and medium-term optimization. The sector's inherent frictions, coupled with advancements in AI and an influx of private equity, make it ripe for new strategies. This indicates a significant upside for diversified real estate conglomerates willing to evolve their operating models and actively seek arbitrage and optionality across their multi-asset portfolios, potentially increasing returns on assets by 3 to 5 percentage points annually.
viewpoints.source_title: Taking a Page from Commodity Traders: A New Playbook for Commercial Real Estate Investors

viewpoints.title: AI poised to transform real estate value chain and operational models
viewpoints.description: McKinsey posits that AI will fundamentally transform real estate, extending beyond traditional property operations to redesign entire business domains. This includes enhancing consumer experience from search to service, optimizing construction processes, and streamlining enterprise functions like procurement and finance. For diversified real estate conglomerates, this signifies a crucial opportunity to reimagine their operating models and achieve significant value creation across their multi-asset portfolios, rather than merely bolting AI onto existing workflows, by creating more responsive and reliable experiences.

viewpoints.title: Europe's construction sector faces weak growth, limiting real estate momentum
viewpoints.description: ING Research anticipates Europe's construction output to grow marginally by 0.5% in 2026, following declines in 2024. Subdued growth in residential and non-residential building, driven by high financing costs, construction expenses, and geopolitical risks, will cap overall momentum. While infrastructure investment offers some offset, diversified real estate conglomerates engaged in multi-asset development will face a challenging environment with limited scope for robust expansion and profitability from new projects across their European portfolios, requiring strategic adjustments to investment and development pipelines.
viewpoints.source_title: Europe's construction sector faces a period of weak growth

demand_drivers.driver: Increased market data and AI/ML capabilities
demand_drivers.description: AI and machine learning advancements make it cheaper to identify arbitrage and value creation opportunities, turning market data into a key differentiator for capturing dark value.
The growing presence of private equity investors who are willing to disrupt traditional operating models encourages a shift towards more dynamic investment strategies.

new_opportunities.description: Identifying and acting on mispricings or temporary market inefficiencies across geographies, asset qualities, and lease terms.
Implementing structured operating models and processes to consistently capture value from shorter-term market dynamics, moving beyond sporadic 'asset flipping'.

market_sizing.methodology: Estimated annual value worldwide lost by commercial real estate investors not capturing short- and medium-term optimization opportunities. This 'dark value' is derived from a theoretical potential for increased returns.
market_sizing.source_title: Taking a Page from Commodity Traders: A New Playbook for Commercial Real Estate Investors

pnl_drivers.description: Systematic capture of short- and medium-term opportunities, including geography-based arbitrage, quality-based arbitrage, time-based optionality in lease structures, faster capital repositioning, maintaining immediate buffers, and diversifying funding bases, can significantly boost returns on assets.

market_sizing.methodology: Analysis indicates commercial real estate players can increase their return on assets by 3 to 5 percentage points per annum by applying all optimization levers. A realistic target for well-suited players is 3 to 4 percentage points, which represents a one-third increase from historical average returns of around 9% (1978-2022, US NCREIF data).
market_sizing.source_title: Taking a Page from Commodity Traders: A New Playbook for Commercial Real Estate Investors

demand_drivers.description: NATO members' pledge to raise defence spending to 3.5% of GDP and 1.5% for infrastructure by 2035 drives demand for related industrial and logistics infrastructure.
EU's aim to procure at least 50% of defence needs from within the EU by 2030, rising to 60% by 2035, necessitates more local manufacturing and associated real estate.

demand_drivers.driver: Expanded stockpiling and supply chain resilience
demand_drivers.description: The need for higher inventory levels and resilient supply chains (e.g., EU Stockpiling Strategy) creates structural demand for secure logistics and industrial space.

new_opportunities.description: Opportunities arise for building and leasing specialized manufacturing facilities, secure storage, distribution centers, R&D parks, science parks, and mixed-use innovation districts to meet defence sector needs.
new_opportunities.opportunity: Development of specialized industrial and logistics space

market_sizing.methodology: Savills estimates an additional 37 million square metres of industrial and logistics demand across Europe and the UK by 2033, assuming NATO members converge to a 3.5% defence spending target over seven years. This is compared to an existing defence-related industrial/logistics space of 35-40 million sq m. JLL estimates total existing industrial and logistics real estate inventory at around 400 million sq m. Green Street offers a more conservative estimate of 26 million sqm of additional defence-related demand through 2035.
market_sizing.source_title: Europe's defence push will boost logistics real estate – but won’t…

demand_drivers.description: The strategic shift towards domestic production of defence goods (munitions, vehicles, drones) requires more manufacturing, assembly, storage, and distribution space.

demand_drivers.driver: Enhanced supply chain resilience and stockpiling
demand_drivers.description: The need for higher inventory levels and secure storage for critical defence goods drives demand for specialized logistics facilities, often on long-term leases.

pnl_drivers.description: The new demand source for logistics and industrial real estate can lead to higher occupancy rates and stable, long-term rental income, particularly for specialized and secure facilities.

new_opportunities.description: While much demand is build-to-own, 20-30% could be leasehold, translating to 0.5-1.25 million sqm of additional annual institutional opportunity, focusing on bespoke defence-related facilities.

market_sizing.methodology: Forecasted annual logistics take-up from the defence sector could rise to between 8-20% of total annual take-up across Europe in the coming years. This range is derived by comparing various demand forecasts (e.g., GARBE's Germany estimate extrapolated to Europe, AXA IM/BNP Paribas estimates) with average annual logistics take-up trends (around 25 million sqm per year).
market_sizing.source_title: Europe's defence push will boost logistics real estate – but won’t…
